text:
Six straight games with a point (four goals, four assists), and Tampa Bay is 7-0-0 at home. Brayden Point is one of the reasons, and the way he's doing it is worth a look.

Start with the legs. NHL EDGE puts his top speed in the 97th percentile and his count of 20 mph bursts in the 99th. At 30, he's still the guy carrying the puck into the zone (67% of his entries last season in Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking) rather than chipping it in. At five-on-five the Lightning own 60.5% of the expected goals with him on, nearly eight points better than without him.

This version shoots more from good spots, too: 1.30 expected goals per 60, up from 1.06 last season. His five goals actually trail those chances by about 1.3, so the streak isn't built on lucky bounces.

One caution: Evolving-Hockey noted his 2025-26 results ran well ahead of his expected value. This start looks sturdier. Our range has him finishing between 58 and 85 points.
headline: Point, at full speed, is cashing in
